name: Regional snack and merch resale online
one_liner: Buy cult-favourite regional or branded snacks and merch at full retail and resell them online to fans who can't get them locally.
customer: Fans and expats who can't reach the store or region
offer: Branded snacks, fudge, seasonal t-shirts and logo merch shipped to the buyer
how_it_makes_money: Retail arbitrage markup on products bought at full retail; best sellers are store-logo items and seasonal shirts
startup_cost: low-medium (inventory and shipping; amount not stated)
evidence: 'Me and my business partner spend millions of dollars a year full retail at this store... and we resell it on the internet at texasnacks.com for a profit' (M6woiZk-KeE)
Best sellers are Buc-ee's logo items; Halloween shirts are a top-3 seller every year (M6woiZk-KeE)
Corporate asked them to stop selling fudge (M6woiZk-KeE)
risks: Depends on one brand's goodwill; they can restrict products
Food safety, shelf life and shipping rules (UK/EU import rules for food)

name: Expiring-domain niche website portfolio
one_liner: Buy strong expiring domains at auction and build niche content sites that earn from ads and affiliate links.
customer: Advertisers via AdSense/ad networks, and affiliate programmes
offer: Niche content websites built on aged or premium domains
how_it_makes_money: Display ads and affiliate commissions; domains can also be resold
startup_cost: low (domain auction prices; amount not stated)
time_to_first_revenue: months (early AdSense earnings were $50/month, then grew to $300/month)
evidence: One site 'makes a little over 50 grand a year. I spent about an hour a month on it maybe' (LZ_bjRV6xx0)
Portfolio pays 'hundreds of thousands of dollars every year', managed in a few hours a week (LZ_bjRV6xx0)
risks: Slow ramp: front-loaded time before income
Google algorithm updates and AI search eating traffic

name: AI-built low-cost clone of expensive vertical SaaS
one_liner: Use AI coding tools to rebuild a narrow version of an overpriced industry SaaS and sell it for a fraction of the price.
customer: SMBs paying high monthly fees for vertical software (e.g. property managers on AppFolio)
offer: A stripped-down SaaS covering the core features
how_it_makes_money: Monthly subscription priced about 90–99% below the incumbent (e.g. $23/month vs $2,300/month)
evidence: 'I built a clone of Appfolio using AI and I know you're paying $2,300 a month. I charge $23 a month' (M3mUNpWD4ow)
'They're going to have competitors that do just as much... for 90 to 99% less. So, why not let it be you?' (M3mUNpWD4ow)
risks: Weak evidence: no customer or revenue numbers shared
Switching costs, data migration and trust in vertical software

name: Short-form clipping farm / clipping campaign service
one_liner: Run networks of accounts that cut and cross-post short clips of a brand or creator's content to drive mass views.
customer: Startups, creators and podcasters who want viral reach
offer: Managed clipping campaign: clips cross-posted across many accounts
how_it_makes_money: Retainer or pay-per-view campaign fees (pricing not stated)
evidence: Cluely content is 'cross-posted across thousands of accounts, generating tens of millions of extra views' (M3mUNpWD4ow)
Host says: 'If anyone listening wants to run my clipping campaign, email me' (M3mUNpWD4ow) — shows demand
risks: Platform rules against spam or coordinated accounts

name: Supply-gap product sourcing for Amazon (tariff angle)
one_liner: Use Jungle Scout and ImportYeti to find niche products where demand outstrips supply and source alternative suppliers as tariffs disrupt incumbents.
customer: Amazon shoppers in niches like baby goods or kitchenware
offer: Private-label or sourced niche physical products
evidence: Weak: method only, no case or revenue — 'pick a niche... use Jungle Scout to see what products... are selling like gangbusters' (LXB5G1zqnGg)
US tariff rate jumped from 2.6% to 22% (LXB5G1zqnGg)

name: Interactive lead-magnet scorecard for business owners
one_liner: Build a diagnostic 'score' quiz for a niche audience that captures leads and sells them into a paid offer.
customer: Small business owners (or businesses buying a lead-gen asset)
offer: Scorecard/assessment lead magnet with a follow-up paid offer
how_it_makes_money: Converts leads into a paid product or service; could also be sold as a done-for-you build
startup_cost: low (Codie's version cost hundreds of thousands, but simple versions are cheap)
evidence: 'I also spent hundreds of thousands of dollars making a lead magnet called the owner score' (NViWUwkXizo)
Weak: no conversion or revenue figures
risks: Weak evidence: a marketing tactic rather than a proven standalone business
Needs a paid offer behind it
